To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimal smoothing schedule is a function of the client buffer size, (ii) the optimal smoothing schedules for all possible buffer sizes can be compactly stored and (iii) the optimal smoothing algorithm is very fast.

(i) the optimal schedule can be computed in a few microseconds; (ii) the optimal schedule for all possible client buffers can be precomputed and stored in a compact manner and can be retrieved in a few microseconds, even when the client buffer size is unknown to the server at transmission time; and (iii) the optimal schedule, once computed, can be recomputed quickly when network jitter estimates change.

(i) it is possible to precompute a compact table of all possible optimal transfer schedules for a given stored compressed video, (ii) it is possible, in the context of client interactivity, to precompute a schedule close to the optimal schedule, (iii) it is possible in practice to precompute and compactly store the optimal schedules for a wide range of network jitter estimates, (iv) it is possible (in practice) to compute the optimal schedule on-line for a given client
